jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Architecture
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director of Enterprise Architecture is a strategic leadership role responsible for defining and advancing SE Health’s enterprise architecture vision. This position establishes architecture discipline as a cornerstone of SE Health’s modernization strategy by aligning technology capabilities with business priorities, enabling digital transformation, and ensuring successful integration of critical platforms such as the digital patient record, people/finance/payroll systems, contact center, service management, and others.

The Director leads enterprise-wide architecture decisions that drive agility, scalability, security, and measurable business outcomes. This includes building and maturing the Enterprise Architecture function, establishing an Architecture Review Board, and delivering a three-year technology roadmap that incorporates strategic platforms, cloud strategy, data and analytics capabilities, integration architecture, and security and compliance posture. The Director ensures successful architecture and integration of platforms such as Alayacare and Workday, while driving adoption of best practices, standards, and governance across technology domains. By translating business objectives into coherent, secure, and sustainable technology designs, the Director plays a critical role in spearheading a digital transformation that enhances the experience of patients, families, employees, and clients, supporting SE Health’s mission of exceptional home and community care.

Primary Accountabilities

Enterprise Architecture Strategy and Governance

Develop and execute an enterprise architecture strategy and multi-year roadmap that enables modernization, interoperability, and alignment with organizational goals, including maximizing value from core enterprise platforms (e.g., Alayacare, Workday).
Establish and lead enterprise architecture governance processes (e.g., an Architecture Review Board or Enterprise Architecture Council) to define standards, manage technical debt, and inform major technology and investment decisions.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the CDO, CIO, CTO, and senior leadership, translating business priorities into sustainable, secure, enterprise-wide technology designs.
Assess and improve enterprise architecture maturity, documenting improvements and outcomes aligned to business KPIs and informing continuous evolution of architecture practices.
Drive mission-critical enterprise architecture and data modernization projects, providing strategic oversight and ensuring integration, scalability, and compliance across platforms and business functions.

Technology, Cloud and Systems Integration Architecture

Lead the architecture, integration, and modernization of core enterprise platforms, including Alayacare, Workday, Procura, ERP, CRM, HRIS, Finance, and scheduling systems, to enable a cohesive and interoperable ecosystem across business and clinical operations.
Define and oversee enterprise reference architectures, integration and data standards, patterns, and roadmaps that promote modernization, automation, analytics enablement, and business process optimization.
Lead modernization efforts to rationalize applications, reduce technical debt, and migrate or retire legacy platforms using a cloud-smart, scalable approach.
Oversee enterprise solution architecture across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments to ensure performance, resilience, security, and cost-efficiency, including multi-cloud strategy across AWS and Azure.
Guide adoption of architectural best practices across security, operational excellence, reliability, performance efficiency, and cost optimization domains.
Review and evaluate solution designs and technology proposals, providing direction and recommendations through architecture governance forums.
Analyze enterprise technology and data architecture requirements to support new applications, system scalability, and platform integrations.

Leadership, People and Continuous Improvement

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing enterprise architecture team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and excellence.
Drive continuous improvement and EA maturity by introducing modern frameworks, methodologies, and tooling (e.g., TOGAF, HOPEX) to enhance consistency, documentation, and solution quality.
Embed security and privacy by design across architecture practices, ensuring adherence to cybersecurity, privacy, and healthcare compliance requirements.
Build strong partnerships with Digital, Security, and Business leaders to influence technology strategy, support demand intake, and ensure alignment of solutions to business needs.
Champion digital transformation and innovation by evaluating emerging technologies (e.g., mobile, IoT, telehealth, AI) and recommending their adoption where they advance SE Health’s mission and services.

Data and Analytics Architecture

Define enterprise data architecture strategies, standards, and models that enable analytics, AI, and data-driven decision-making across the organization.
Partner with Data & Analytics teams to design and evolve data platforms (e.g., data lake/warehouse) to support enterprise information management, governance, reporting, and advanced analytics.
Provide leadership, guidance, and mentoring to data architecture and solution design teams on data and integration best practices.
Collaborate with data science and analytics teams to support AI-enabled insights, intelligent automation, and emerging technologies that drive value for clinical and business functions.

AI, Automation & Intelligent Systems

Lead integration of AI-driven insights and intelligent automation into enterprise applications and workflows.
Partner with data science teams to enable machine learning, predictive analytics, and data-driven optimization across clinical and business functions.
Evaluate emerging AI/automation technologies and define architectural guardrails for safe, ethical, and scalable adoption.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field. Experience with EA frameworks (e.g., TOGAF, ArchiMate, or similar) is preferred.
12+ years of experience in enterprise/solution architecture, including leading modernization and large-scale integration initiatives in complex environments.
5+ years of leadership experience managing architecture teams, building high-performing technical talent, and advancing enterprise architecture maturity.
Strong expertise across enterprise, application, data, and technology architecture, with hands-on experience in cloud and integration architectures (AWS/Azure, APIs, microservices, event-driven design).
Experience leading architecture for major SaaS platforms (e.g., CRM, ERP, HR systems); Alayacare and/or Workday strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of data architecture, governance, and analytics enablement; experience with AI/ML-enabled solutions is an asset.
Knowledge of security, privacy, and compliance considerations for enterprise platforms and data.
Experience in healthcare or other highly regulated industries is an asset.
Exceptional communication, consulting, and stakeholder engagement skills, with proven ability to influence executives and simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences.

Why join SE Health?

Competitive Total Rewards So much more than a paycheque! Enjoy comprehensive benefits, pension, flexible pay options, car-loan support, housing solutions and exclusive staff perks.
Flexibility & Belonging Thrive with hybrid work, flexible scheduling and a supportive, inclusive culture that puts people first.
Purpose & Impact Join a national social enterprise where your voice matters. Every role helps advance health, spark innovation and strengthen communities across Canada.
Growth That Meets Your Ambition Access tuition support, training and meaningful career pathways across a growing, future-focused organization.

About SE Health

SE Health is a not-for-profit social enterprise advancing health with heart. With 115+ years of impact, we bring hope, happiness and exceptional care to people and communities across Canada. We lead with empathy, dignity and purpose while building a future where everyone can realize their full health and well-being potential. We’re also an inclusive, supportive workplace offering competitive compensation, strong benefits and real opportunities to grow. We’re All In Together.

jobs.description:
Join CoolIT, an Ecolab Company, a global leader in Direct Liquid Cooling technology for data centers, supercomputers, and high-performance computing environments.

CoolIT is seeking a Director of Enterprise Architecture
to provide the architectural vision and strategic technology leadership needed to support our future growth. You will partner with senior business and technology leaders to translate strategic priorities into integrated process, data, and technology strategies, target-state architectures, and multi-year roadmaps.

This is a forward-looking, director-level position focused on shaping long-term architecture decisions rather than providing day-to-day operational support. You will guide enterprise resource planning modernization, including NetSuite and the broader enterprise application landscape, while establishing

technology direction for Manufacturing and the Integrated Supply Chain in alignment with Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial capabilities. You will also evaluate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, software-as-a-service solutions, automation, Industrial Internet of Things, and cloud and edge technologies, to determine how they can support the future of work and deliver measurable business value.

What You Will Do

Partner with Enterprise Business Engagement Managers and Business Relationship Managers to translate business priorities into integrated process, data, and technology strategies, capability roadmaps, and investment priorities.
Develop and maintain three-to-five-year technology roadmaps for enterprise resource planning, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and other key enterprise functions.
Establish the enterprise resource planning modernization strategy for NetSuite evolution, capability optimization, application simplification, and future-state architecture.
Define technology strategies and target-state architectures for Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Digital Plant capabilities in alignment with Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial priorities.
Collaborate with Solution Architects and Platform Architects to develop reference, target-state, and transition architectures spanning business processes, technology platforms, data, integration, security, and infrastructure.
Lead application rationalization and modernization initiatives that reduce technical debt, duplication, unnecessary customization, and complexity across the enterprise application landscape.
Evaluate and guide the strategic adoption of artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, automation, data and analytics, Industrial Internet of Things, software-as-a-service solutions, and cloud and edge technologies.
Participate in future-of-work discussions and identify emerging technology opportunities that can improve productivity, resilience, scalability, and sustainability.
Oversee architecture governance and strategic technology decisions while ensuring alignment with established enterprise architecture principles, frameworks, and standards.
Advise and influence senior business and technology leaders by connecting business strategy, architectural direction, technology investment, and execution.

Position Details

This is a director-level position focused primarily on architectural vision, future growth, emerging technologies, and long-term strategic roadmaps rather than day-to-day operational support.
The position requires an understanding of operational considerations, including cybersecurity, platform support, reliability, and service continuity, to ensure that future-state architecture decisions are practical and sustainable.
Work arrangement: Hybrid in Calgary, AB.
Travel requirements: 10% or less

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline.
12 years of progressively responsible technology and architecture experience.
5 years of experience in architecture or technology leadership.
Experience developing enterprise strategies, target-state architectures, and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Experience developing enterprise resource planning strategies and leading modernization initiatives, ideally involving NetSuite and exposure to large-scale enterprise resource planning platforms.
Experience with Supply Chain and Manufacturing capabilities and cross-functional Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial processes and platforms.
Knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks, principles, and practices across business processes, technology platforms, data, integration, cybersecurity, and infrastructure.
Experience developing business capability models, reference architectures, target-state architectures, and transition roadmaps.
Experience applying data, integration, cloud and edge, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity architecture principles.
Experience influencing senior business and technology leaders and guiding strategic technology decisions across organizational boundaries.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading a major enterprise resource planning modernization or transformation program involving NetSuite, SAP, Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, or Microsoft Dynamics 365.
Enterprise architecture design experience across Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial functions.
Experience with Smart Manufacturing, Digital Plant, and Industrial Internet of Things technologies.
Knowledge of process and discrete manufacturing environments, including batch manufacturing, formulation management, lot traceability, quality, product stewardship, and regulatory compliance.
Practical experience applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, or intelligent automation to enterprise business processes.
Experience evaluating and implementing software-as-a-service platforms and emerging enterprise technologies.
Knowledge of The Open Group Architecture Framework, ArchiMate, capability-based planning, and architecture governance.
Demonstrated ability to connect strategy and execution, influence across organizational boundaries, and advise senior leaders as a trusted partner.

Founded in Calgary, Alberta in 2001, CoolIT Systems is the leading Direct Liquid Cooling technology provider for data centers, supercomputers, and desktop computers. We design and manufacture solutions used by the largest tech companies globally.

Recognized as one of “The Americas’ Fastest Growing Companies 2023” by Financial Times and honored with the Deloitte Fast 50 Clean Technology award in 2022, as well as the Deloitte Fast 500 distinction in both 2021 and 2022, CoolIT's rapid growth is capturing global attention.

jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

The Role

The Managing Director, Technology Architecture & Governance is accountable for setting and governing CPP Investments’ enterprise technology architecture, As Managing Director, Technology Architecture & Governance, you will set and govern CPP Investments’ enterprise technology architecture, engineering practices and lifecycle standards, helping ensure the Fund operates on a resilient, modern and sustainable technology foundation.

Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Technology & Data, you will provide practical, outcome-focused direction on architecture, technical debt, technology lifecycle management and engineering excellence. This enterprise leadership role has no direct reports and operates through influence, deep technical expertise, sound judgement and effective governance.

The Team

Technology & Data helps enable CPP Investments’ investment strategies and supports the Fund’s day-to-day operations through enterprise technology and data capabilities. Within the department, the Technology Architecture & Governance mandate provides enterprise-wide direction for architecture, engineering practices and technology lifecycle management, partnering across the Fund to strengthen resilience, scalability, cost efficiency and delivery effectiveness.

Accountabilities

Define and maintain the enterprise technology architecture, capability model and capability roadmap aligned to CPP Investments’ mandate, One Fund strategy, and long-term business objectives.
Provide clear architectural direction that balances innovation, resilience, security, and cost efficiency across the enterprise.
Lead lightweight, decision-oriented architecture governance focused on unblocking teams and resolving trade-offs, rather than enforcing rigid controls.
Provide timely, well-reasoned guidance on complex design choices, ensuring alignment across platforms while enabling local autonomy where appropriate.
Act as a senior problem solver for the enterprise, engaging directly in the most complex, ambiguous, and high-impact business problems and technology challenges.
Bring systems thinking and deep technical judgement to diagnose root causes, shape options, and guide decisions that balance near-term outcomes with long-term sustainability.
Own the enterprise approach to technology lifecycle management, including currency, obsolescence, and vendor dependency risk.
Define strategies to identify, prioritize, and systematically reduce technical debt, improving platform stability, maintainability, and total cost of ownership over time.
Set enterprise expectations for software development lifecycle, engineering excellence, and ways of working including agile practices.
Drive continuous improvement in how technology is designed, built, tested, and released, enabling predictable delivery, higher quality outcomes, and faster time to value

What You Bring

Undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field required
Advanced education or professional certifications in architecture, cloud, or engineering practices considered an asset
Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in technology architecture, engineering leadership, or enterprise technology roles
Demonstrated success leading large-scale technology decisions and standards in complex organizations
Experience in financial services, investment management, or other complex enterprises is preferred
Deep expertise in engineering, enterprise architecture, modern technology platforms, and large-scale system design
Strong understanding of cloud-native architecture, integration patterns, modern data achitecture, and security principles
Proven experience establishing and governing software development lifecycle, engineering standards, and agile practices
Expertise in technology lifecycle management, vendor strategy, and technical debt remediation
Understanding of financial services or large, complex enterprises and their regulatory and risk environments

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

Technology is one of the most important parts of Warner Music Group’s business. Whether it is supporting artists and songwriters, delivering accurate royalty and performance data to global partners, or giving creative and business teams modern data and AI tools, engineering makes it possible.

jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. jobs.title: AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance
jobs.description:
As AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance
, you will lead the strategy, governance and enablement required to accelerate responsible adoption of AI and strengthen data capabilities across Actuarial.

Reporting to the VP, Actuarial Innovation, you will partner with Actuarial leaders, enterprise AI and Data teams, Data Governance, Technology, Risk and other partners to establish and embed data governance, along with lead the shift from individual AI use cases to embedding AI and trusted data into core actuarial workflows and ways of working.

You will lead the evolution of Actuarial data governance, establishing clear ownership and stewardship, strengthening data quality management, and creating greater transparency and accountability for the data that underpins critical actuarial processes. You will work across Actuarial and enterprise partners to ensure data issues are identified, prioritized and addressed, while aligning Actuarial practices with broader enterprise data standards and governance.

You will also establish the frameworks and capabilities that enable Actuarial to innovate responsibly and at scale, including AI portfolio prioritization, citizen-led development, responsible AI governance, capability building and value realization. You will provide a trusted view of the Actuarial AI portfolio and help leaders determine where to invest, accelerate, scale, redirect or stop initiatives based on business value, feasibility and risk.

The role will be instrumental in developing an AI- and data-enabled actuarial function, improving productivity, quality and speed of insight while strengthening the governance and accountability required to maintain trust in actuarial data and AI-enabled processes.

Position Responsibilities

AI & Data Strategy and Transformation

Develop and execute the Actuarial AI and Data strategy, aligned with broader Actuarial priorities and enterprise AI, Data and Technology strategies.
Partner with Actuarial leaders to identify and redesign priority workflows where AI, automation and better use of data can materially improve how actuarial work is performed.
Establish a clear roadmap for AI and Data capability development, balancing near-term opportunities with longer-term transformation priorities.

AI Portfolio Governance & Value Realization

Establish and evolve a transparent governance and prioritization framework for the Actuarial AI portfolio, including intake, assessment, prioritization, decision rights and pathways for delivery.
Maintain a trusted view of the AI portfolio, including strategic alignment, expected value, delivery progress, dependencies, risks and realized outcomes.
Lead structured portfolio reviews and provide recommendations on which opportunities should be accelerated, scaled, redirected, paused or stopped.
Develop and maintain a value-realization framework with measurable baselines and outcomes,

AI Enablement, Adoption & Capability Building

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Vice President, Finance (“VP Finance”) is a senior finance leader accountable for the integrity, accuracy, and effectiveness of accounting, reporting, and financial operations across both Sirius entities: Sirius Instrumentation and Controls Inc. (Canadian parent) and Sirius Controls Inc. (U.S. subsidiary). The VP Finance also partners closely with leaders across the Company to strengthen effectiveness and optimize performance.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”), the VP Finance serves as the CFO’s deputy and designated backup, ensuring continuity across board, sponsor, lender, banking, insurance, and audit relationships, and acting on the CFO’s behalf as delegated or required.

The VP Finance retains direct ownership of the accounting function while progressively delegating close and transactional execution to the Assistant Controller as that role continues to develop. The scope will expand across financial planning and analysis, treasury, tax compliance coordination, and strategic finance, including key initiatives such as ERP implementation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

In support of the organization's strategic objectives, the successful candidate will be accountable for the following key responsibilities:

Financial Reporting and Technical Accounting

Accountable for the consolidated month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close across both entities, including intercompany eliminations and FX translation (IAS 21); ensure timely, accurate consolidated reporting under IFRS.
Accountable for all IFRS technical positions including but not limited to - IFRS 15 revenue recognition, IAS 2 standard costing and WIP valuation, IFRS 16 leases, IAS 12 deferred tax, and IFRS 3 acquisition accounting carry-forward; prepare technical memos and defend positions to auditors.
Responsible for the primary external audit relationship - planning, PBC management, technical defense, and year-end coordination.
Ensure compliance with tax, regulatory, and Board of Directors-specific reporting requirements.

Internal Controls, Risk, and Governance

Responsible for the internal control environment across all transactional cycles (revenue/receivables, purchases/payables, payroll, inventory, fixed assets, treasury, close and reporting); and progress the framework toward SOX-lite (COSO 2013).
Establish and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and controls documentation.
Partner with the CFO on risk management and audit committee reporting.

Accounting Operations and Delegation

Accountable for the accuracy and completeness of accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, inventory, and treasury activities across both entities.
Progressively transition close execution, transactional review and AR/AP Admins to the Assistant Controller against a defined development plan, retaining review authority and overall accountability for the function.
Supervise tax compliance - GST/HST, U.S. state sales and use tax, and cross-border requirements-coordinating with external advisors on transfer pricing, withholding, and treaty application.
Collaborating with sales department, legal counsel and clients to ensure timely and optimal Master Services Agreements.

Financial Planning and Analysis; Board and Sponsor Reporting

Responsible for the completion of the board reporting packages: monthly flash, quarterly board pack, sponsor reporting, and covenant compliance certificates.
Build and lead the FP&A capability - annual budget, rolling 12-month forecast (quarterly), budget-versus-actual and variance analysis, and KPI reporting - to support decision-making.
Assume Budget Master role while partnering with the CFO to deliver the annual budget.
Provide insight on financial performance, margins, working capital, and risk areas as a Partner to the executive team.

Treasury and Cash Management

Responsible for working capital management, and CAD/USD exposure monitoring.
Manage day-to-day banking relationships, credit facility reporting, and intercompany funding, escalating covenant and liquidity matters to the CFO.

Systems and Process Improvement

Lead the finance workstreams of the ERP implementation - requirements, chart of accounts design, data migration, UAT, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization - through the transition from QuickBooks.
Collaborate with supporting the Plant Controller and Senior Vice President Operations, operationalize standard costing in the make-to-order manufacturing environment, including BOM accuracy, overhead absorption, and variance analysis.
Drive process automation and continuous improvement of the close, reporting cadence, and documentation base to support margin improvement.

Leadership and Team Development

Manage, mentor, and scale the accounting team; foster a culture of accountability, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration.
Develop the Assistant Controller on a defined succession track toward financial controller-level ownership of the close; establish SOPs, training milestones, and cross-training pairs.
Build a documented and defensible finance function.

Strategic Partnership and CFO Redundancy

Act as the CFO’s deputy: represent Finance with the board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as delegated, and assume the CFO’s operating responsibilities in the CFO’s absence.
Support M&A activity - diligence, integration, and acquisition accounting - including vendor due diligence and quality of earnings readiness.
Support international expansion structuring (Middle East and beyond) with external advisors as it progresses.
Collaborate with the sales, operations, and engineering teams, to be a Business Partner supporting financial decision making, cost savings initiatives, and strategic decision making

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Audit-Ready Financial Reporting:
Consolidated IFRS reporting is delivered accurately and on schedule, with a clean external audit and no material adjustments or control deficiencies.
Scalable, Audit-Ready Finance Function:
Strong controls, clear documentation, and a successfully implemented ERP that position the business well.
Seamless CFO Continuity and Team Succession:
The VP Finance is trusted by the Board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as the CFO’s deputy, while the Assistant Controller progresses to independent ownership of the close.

THE INDIVIDUAL

Given the pivotal role this individual will be expected to play in achieving the strategic objectives of the company and in supporting the success of the organization, it is essential that the successful candidate possess the following education, experience, competencies and attributes:

Education

A university degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field is required; an MBA is considered an asset.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing is required.
Strong working knowledge of IFRS is required, including the application of complex technical accounting standards.
Knowledge of U.S. GAAP or cross-border reporting experience would be considered an asset.
Commitment to ongoing professional development, particularly in IFRS, tax, and financial systems.

Experience

Must-have:

A minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including senior leadership responsibility for the accounting and reporting function.
Demonstrated expertise in IFRS, including consolidated reporting across multiple entities, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and preparation of technical accounting positions.
Proven experience leading the external audit relationship and delivering clean, timely audits.
Track record of building and strengthening internal controls, accounting policies, and finance processes.
Experience preparing Board, lender, or investor reporting, including budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis.
Demonstrated success leading, mentoring, and developing accounting teams, including succession planning and delegation.

Nice-to-have:

Manufacturing experience is strongly preferred, ideally within a make-to-order or engineered products environment, with a solid understanding of standard costing, inventory valuation, and overhead absorption.
Experience in a private equity-backed or sponsor-owned organization, vendor due diligence, or quality of earnings processes.
Experience leading or supporting an ERP implementation, particularly a transition from an entry-level system such as QuickBooks.
Exposure to U.S. GAAP and cross-border Canada/U.S. operations, including sales and use tax, transfer pricing, and withholding considerations.

Le ou la Directeur(trice), Financement de projets
dirige les activités de financement des projets de centres de données et d'infrastructures énergétiques du Groupe ADAG, depuis la levée de capitaux initiale jusqu'à la phase de construction, puis d'exploitation. Cette personne est responsable du modèle financier des projets et de la gestion quotidienne des relations avec les prêteurs, les investisseurs et leurs conseillers.

En joignant le Groupe Adag, vous intégrerez une équipe dynamique et ambitieuse qui vous permettra d'apprendre, de vous développer et de progresser professionnellement
. Notre organisation est en pleine croissance et transforme son industrie tout en misant sur une culture de collaboration et de plaisir au travail. Si vous êtes reconnu(e) pour votre sens de l'organisation, votre rigueur et votre capacité à mobiliser les gens, nous aimerions vous rencontrer !

Rôle, responsabilités et objectifs

Développer, maintenir et être responsable du modèle financier de projet répondant aux exigences des prêteurs, ainsi que coordonner son audit indépendant.
Diriger l'exécution des financements par dette et par capitaux propres, incluant la préparation du mémorandum d'information, la gestion de la salle de données (data room), les vérifications diligentes des prêteurs et la négociation des feuilles de modalités (term sheets).
Collaborer avec les conseillers juridiques, l'ingénieur indépendant, les agences de notation et les preneurs fermes jusqu'à la clôture financière des projets.
Évaluer la bancabilité des baux de locataires, des ententes d'approvisionnement énergétique et des contrats de construction, et intégrer les résultats aux négociations commerciales.
Après la clôture du financement, gérer les décaissements de construction, le suivi des coûts à terminer (cost-to-complete), le respect des clauses financières (covenants) et les obligations de reporting auprès des prêteurs.
Élaborer des structures de financement et des plans de capitalisation pour les futurs campus de centres de données et projets énergétiques.
Recruter, encadrer et développer une équipe spécialisée en financement de projets.

Ce que vous apportez à l'organisation

Plus de 10 ans d'expérience en financement de projets, en banque d'investissement spécialisée en infrastructures ou en investissement dans les infrastructures.
Expérience démontrée dans la réalisation de financements majeurs sans recours (non-recourse) ou à haut rendement (high-yield). Une expérience dans les secteurs des centres de données, de l'énergie ou des énergies renouvelables est fortement privilégiée.
Expert(e) en modélisation financière, capable de présenter et de défendre un modèle financier devant des prêteurs et des agences de notation.
Excellente connaissance des structures de dette, des clauses financières (covenants), des comptes de réserve et du financement de la construction.
Le titre de CFA
ou un MBA
constitue un atout.
Excellente maîtrise de l'anglais. La connaissance du français constitue un atout.

Mode de travail

Ce poste suit un mode de travail hybride nécessitant une présence régulière au bureau :
Présence obligatoire au bureau trois (3) jours par semaine
.
Les lundis et les vendredis sont des journées obligatoires en présentiel.

Pourquoi vous joindre à nous?

Une équipe jeune, expérimentée et dynamique, avec un club social actif.
Un horaire de travail flexible.
Un régime d'avantages sociaux et dentaires généreux.
Un minimum de 3 semaines de vacances
.
L'opportunité d'évoluer au sein d'une organisation en pleine croissance.

Qui sommes-nous?
Fondé en 2020, le Groupe Adag
répond à la demande croissante pour les centres de données et les infrastructures critiques, stimulée par l'essor du télétravail, des services infonuagiques et de l'intelligence artificielle. Forts d'une présence au Canada et aux États-Unis, nous offrons une gamme complète de services spécialisés en centres de données dans ces régions.

De la gestion de projet à la conception, en passant par la modélisation CFD et l'approvisionnement, nous intégrons des pratiques durables à chacune de nos solutions afin d'aider nos clients à répondre à leurs besoins opérationnels tout en réduisant leur impact environnemental.

Chez le Groupe Adag, nous sommes fiers de notre agilité, qui nous permet de réaliser des projets dans des délais serrés tout en maintenant les plus hauts standards de qualité. Nous nous engageons à façonner l'avenir des solutions de centres de données en plaçant la durabilité au cœur de notre approche. Joignez-vous à nous et construisons l'avenir ensemble!

Chez Adag, nous favorisons un milieu de travail inclusif où chaque personne a l'occasion de s'épanouir et d'atteindre son plein potentiel. Nous vous encourageons à être vous-même au travail. Nous accueillons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées et serons heureux d'évaluer votre profil dans le cadre de notre processus de recrutement. Nous vous remercions de votre intérêt envers Adag. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes retenues pour une entrevue seront contactées.

The Director of Project Finance
leads the financing of ADAG's data centre and power projects, from the first raise through construction and into operations. This role owns the project financial model and the day-to-day relationships with lenders, investors and their advisers.

jobs.description:
Vice President, Supply Chain & Inventory Management

About Delta Group

Delta Group is a Western Canadian wholesale distribution and solutions platform serving waterworks and water infrastructure, agricultural irrigation, pumps and motors, water treatment, wastewater and related markets. Delta combines multi-branch wholesale distribution with specialist technical solutions, engineered systems, projects and service. Through acquisitions and organic growth, the group has an opportunity to integrate supply-chain practices while maintaining the market knowledge and relationships of its operating businesses.

Position mandate

Lead Delta’s end-to-end group supply-chain strategy, with executive accountability for procurement, inventory investment and quality, demand planning, vendor economics, replenishment and network efficiency. Build one disciplined operating framework across multiple companies and branches without impairing customer service or project execution. This is an operational change-leadership position, not simply a senior purchasing appointment. This role can be based in Calgary or Chilliwack, BC.

Group supply-chain strategy and governance

Design and implement group-wide policies for inventory, purchasing, approvals, stock allocation and supplier engagement.
Clarify central versus local authority, escalation rules, exception management and performance accountability.
Partner closely with General Managers, Finance, sales and operations; lead monthly supply-chain performance reviews.
Integrate acquired businesses and branch practices into a scalable operating model.

Inventory investment, productivity and controls

Own group inventory productivity, target-setting and action plans by branch, segment, category and SKU.
Drive reduction of excess, obsolete, slow-moving and duplicate inventory through transfers, vendor returns, disposition and prevention.
Set service-sensitive reorder points, safety stocks, inventory classifications and replenishment policies.
Establish consistent cycle counts, inventory accuracy and inventory ownership controls; coordinate valuation and reserves with Finance.
Protect strategic, seasonal and critical long-lead stock while improving inventory turns and cash generation.

Procurement and supplier management

Coordinate category strategy, purchasing scale, approval limits and controls for committed purchases.
Negotiate supplier terms, pricing, rebates, freight, returns, vendor-managed/consignment arrangements and service commitments.
Implement supplier scorecards and contingency planning for critical products and manufacturers.
Improve purchase-order visibility, interbranch-first decisions and special-order controls; prevent unsupported speculative buys.
Maintain the relationships needed to protect exclusive lines and the commercial advantage of Delta’s technical product portfolios.

Demand planning and major projects

Create rolling forecasting processes using sales patterns, seasonality, known projects and credible customer commitments.
Differentiate recurring wholesale replenishment from project-specific purchasing for pivots, pipe, pumps and engineered packages.
Coordinate purchasing with project managers, installation schedules, deposits and supplier lead times.
Manage cancellations, unallocated project material, foreign-exchange and supply risks through clear ownership and exit plans.

Warehousing, distribution and logistics

Evaluate branch stocking, regional hubs, stock transfers, warehousing productivity and freight economics.
Standardize receiving, storage, picking, shipping and transfers where it creates measurable value.
Build evidence-based business cases for any warehouse consolidation, logistics outsourcing or network redesign.

Systems, master data and analytics

Serve as executive business owner for supply-chain processes.
Establish item-master governance: duplicates, naming, UOMs, vendor references, product attributes, inactive SKUs and status.
Build reliable dashboards for aging, turns, fill rate, demand accuracy, outstanding POs, project stock and supplier performance.
Drive practical system-based replenishment and useful automation rather than spreadsheets without accountability.

Working capital and financial accountability

Develop annual and rolling plans for inventory cash release, purchasing efficiencies and inventory-related operating costs.
Coordinate with VP Finance on cash forecasting, open commitments, vendor terms and independently verified savings.
Evaluate investments against inventory carrying cost, service levels, gross margin, liquidity and project risks.
Report monthly to the CEO with financial outcomes, constraints and corrective actions.

People leadership and transformation

Assess and develop existing branch purchasing, inventory and supply-chain employees; recommend an appropriate group structure.
Hire, coach and hold accountable functional leaders and analysts as approved.
Work constructively with GMs while challenging unsupported inventory and purchasing decisions.
Lead branch-level adoption through training, site visits, clear metrics and consistent follow-through.

Required experience and qualifications

12–15+ years of relevant progression in supply chain, inventory, procurement or wholesale distribution operations, including at least five in a senior multi-branch leadership role.
Demonstrable responsibility for material inventory investment across multiple branches, with quantified improvements in turns, aged inventory, cash flow and service.
Strong track record in vendor negotiations, category strategy, purchase controls and operational change after acquisitions.
Commercial understanding of distribution gross margin, inventory carrying cost, cash conversion, stockouts and service economics.
Hands-on experience implementing effective ERP-based replenishment and master-data management.
Ability to lead effectively through influence and formal authority in decentralized technical distribution businesses.
Relevant degree or equivalent operating experience; SCMP, CSCP or CPIM an asset; regular Western Canadian travel required.

Preferred background

Industrial, waterworks, plumbing, pump and motor, agricultural equipment, irrigation, electrical or HVAC wholesale distribution; acquisition integration; regional distribution network optimization; and balancing project procurement with standard branch replenishment.
Leadership profile
Commercially astute, financially disciplined and decisive; credible at branch and warehouse level; analytically strong, capable of difficult conversations with respected GMs, and equally focused on supplier relationships, customer service and sustainable cash release. Comfortable with ambiguous data but unwilling to accept unsupported conclusions.

Key measures of success

Inventory investment and turns by business, branch and category, adjusted for commercial conditions and service needs.
Aged, obsolete and duplicate stock reduction; inventory accuracy and shrinkage.
Working-capital release and annualized procurement/freight/rebate savings validated by Finance.
Customer fill rates, on-time delivery, backorders and project material availability.
Purchasing compliance, forecasting reliability, supplier performance and inventory transfer effectiveness.
Business Central item-master quality, supply-chain reporting and adoption of replenishment processes.
Strength and accountability of supply-chain leadership and branch operating practices.

First-year priorities

First 30 days: establish validated baselines, purchasing commitment visibility, risk/opportunity ranking and assessment of current team. By 90 days: institute buying authority, interbranch-first controls, aged-inventory program and CEO dashboard. Months 4–6: demonstrate measurable cash release, supplier and forecasting improvements. By 12 months: deliver sustained financial and service outcomes and an approved second-year improvement plan. Specific financial targets will be agreed with the CEO and VP Finance after verifying opening conditions.

Why join Delta

The opportunity is to shape the supply-chain economics of a substantial Western Canadian technical distribution platform, turn scale into meaningful procurement and inventory advantage, and build a disciplined, scalable organization. The role carries senior leadership visibility, operating influence and direct accountability for measurable results.

jobs.description:
Overview

The High‑Risk Portfolio Management Team (HRPMT) enhances CCB’s overall risk oversight capabilities by providing specialized expertise, advisory support, and strategic guidance for accounts exhibiting deteriorating financial performance, emerging risk indicators, or complex credit concerns. Unlike traditional credit roles, HRPMT operates in a consulting and advisory capacity
, supporting the commercial banking lines of business with expert insights to strengthen the management of high‑risk, watch‑list, and impaired accounts.

The team works closely with relationship managers, credit partners, and leadership to ensure early identification of risk, informed decision‑making, and strong discipline around the oversight of vulnerable segments of the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Specialized Risk Assessment & Advisory Support

Conducts advanced financial analysis and risk assessments of clients demonstrating signs of weakness or deterioration, providing the LOB with actionable insights and recommended risk‑mitigation strategies.
Offers guidance on appropriate structures, terms, and risk controls for high‑risk accounts, ensuring alignment with bank policies, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Advises on complex or distressed credit situations, including covenant breaches, liquidity concerns, operational challenges, and industry‑driven pressures.
Supports LOB teams with strategies for managing watch‑list, impaired, and emerging‑risk accounts, including exit strategies, recovery pathways, and restructuring options.

High‑Risk Portfolio Oversight

Performs enhanced portfolio monitoring to detect early‑warning signals, covenant non‑compliance, or deteriorating credit trends.
Evaluates portfolio‑level performance indicators and risk concentrations, escalating concerns where appropriate and recommending corrective actions.
Assesses the overall quality of risk management practices across the high‑risk portfolio, identifying gaps and recommending improvements.

Subject Matter Expertise & Consultancy

Operates as a specialist resource to senior leaders and frontline teams, supporting decision‑making on complex or ambiguous credit scenarios.
Provides expertise for the review of high‑risk transactions, challenging underlying assumptions, and advising on risk‑aligned alternatives.
Engages with internal stakeholders to ensure consistency in the management of high‑risk exposures across the enterprise.

Governance, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Strengthens discipline and transparency around watch‑list and impaired account management procedures.
Implements adjustments to risk oversight strategies in response to shifting market, economic, or client‑specific conditions.
Contributes to enterprise initiatives that enhance risk governance, improve monitoring capabilities, and support proactive portfolio management.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partners closely with Commercial banking stakeholders to support their management of deteriorating clients while maintaining LOB ownership of BAU underwriting and client relationships.
Supports senior leadership with insights, analysis, and recommendations to inform capital allocation decisions and risk appetite considerations.
Engages with industry peers and internal networks to stay informed on emerging risks, competitive trends, and evolving best practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience in credit, lending, restructuring, portfolio management, or financial analysis within a corporate or banking environment.
Strong credit qualifications, including deep knowledge of commercial credit structures, deteriorating‑credit dynamics, and high‑risk portfolio management practices.
Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred (Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field).
Demonstrated ability to assess complex financial situations, identify risks, and recommend solutions aligned with risk appetite and enterprise policies.
Proven capability to operate in an advisory role, influence stakeholders, and provide expertise in non‑routine, ambiguous, or sensitive credit situations.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgment under pressure.

$85,500.00 - $185,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

THE ORGANIZATION

Sirius designs and manufactures chemical injection systems and instrumentation packages for upstream and midstream oil and gas operators. Their equipment runs in some of the harshest production environments in the world - Western Canada, the Permian, and increasingly the Middle East, Africa and Latin America - where precision matters and downtime costs money. Their technologies help eliminate greenhouse gas emissions, improve injection accuracy, and reduce manpower and chemical costs - two of their customers’ largest expenses. The portfolio includes solar-powered and AC chemical injection systems, environmentally friendly tank systems, and advanced automation technologies.

Founded in April 2003 in Alberta, Canada, Sirius is headquartered in Edmonton with U.S. operations in Midland, Texas (operating as Sirius Controls Inc.) since 2017. Sirius is a registered corporation with APEGA (Association of Professional Engineers) and was awarded the 2018 “Clean Technology Innovation” Award by CETAC-West. Since December 2024, Sirius has been backed by a private equity sponsor and is executing a multi-year growth plan that targets a doubling of revenue across both countries, while adding key international markets.

Sirius’s Core Values define their culture, drive their work, and guide their commitment to excellence. They are the operating standard for every member of the team - and the Vice President, Finance is expected to model and reinforce them.

Core Values:

Continuous Innovation
: Innovation begins with listening to understand and transforms curiosity into impactful solutions. It is a continuous improvement loop that channels learning back into our products, processes, and people.
Integrity:
We do what we say we will do. We take responsibility for our actions and own our commitments to become trusted advisors that clients rely on.
Collaboration:
We achieve excellence by working together with trust, humility, open communication, and a shared purpose. Collaboration means ownership across every step of the process.

For more information on Sirius Instrumentation & Controls, please visit their website at: https://www.siriuscontrols.com/.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Vice President, Finance (“VP Finance”) is a senior finance leader accountable for the integrity, accuracy, and effectiveness of accounting, reporting, and financial operations across both Sirius entities: Sirius Instrumentation and Controls Inc. (Canadian parent) and Sirius Controls Inc. (U.S. subsidiary). The VP Finance also partners closely with leaders across the Company to strengthen effectiveness and optimize performance.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”), the VP Finance serves as the CFO’s deputy and designated backup, ensuring continuity across board, sponsor, lender, banking, insurance, and audit relationships, and acting on the CFO’s behalf as delegated or required.

The VP Finance retains direct ownership of the accounting function while progressively delegating close and transactional execution to the Assistant Controller as that role continues to develop. The scope will expand across financial planning and analysis, treasury, tax compliance coordination, and strategic finance, including key initiatives such as ERP implementation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

In support of the organization's strategic objectives, the successful candidate will be accountable for the following key responsibilities:

Financial Reporting and Technical Accounting

Accountable for the consolidated month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close across both entities, including intercompany eliminations and FX translation (IAS 21); ensure timely, accurate consolidated reporting under IFRS.
Accountable for all IFRS technical positions including but not limited to - IFRS 15 revenue recognition, IAS 2 standard costing and WIP valuation, IFRS 16 leases, IAS 12 deferred tax, and IFRS 3 acquisition accounting carry-forward; prepare technical memos and defend positions to auditors.
Responsible for the primary external audit relationship - planning, PBC management, technical defense, and year-end coordination.
Ensure compliance with tax, regulatory, and Board of Directors-specific reporting requirements.

Internal Controls, Risk, and Governance

Responsible for the internal control environment across all transactional cycles (revenue/receivables, purchases/payables, payroll, inventory, fixed assets, treasury, close and reporting); and progress the framework toward SOX-lite (COSO 2013).
Establish and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and controls documentation.
Partner with the CFO on risk management and audit committee reporting.

Accounting Operations and Delegation

Accountable for the accuracy and completeness of accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, inventory, and treasury activities across both entities.
Progressively transition close execution, transactional review and AR/AP Admins to the Assistant Controller against a defined development plan, retaining review authority and overall accountability for the function.
Supervise tax compliance - GST/HST, U.S. state sales and use tax, and cross-border requirements-coordinating with external advisors on transfer pricing, withholding, and treaty application.
Collaborating with sales department, legal counsel and clients to ensure timely and optimal Master Services Agreements.

Financial Planning and Analysis; Board and Sponsor Reporting

Responsible for the completion of the board reporting packages: monthly flash, quarterly board pack, sponsor reporting, and covenant compliance certificates.
Build and lead the FP&A capability - annual budget, rolling 12-month forecast (quarterly), budget-versus-actual and variance analysis, and KPI reporting - to support decision-making.
Assume Budget Master role while partnering with the CFO to deliver the annual budget.
Provide insight on financial performance, margins, working capital, and risk areas as a Partner to the executive team.

Treasury and Cash Management

Responsible for working capital management, and CAD/USD exposure monitoring.
Manage day-to-day banking relationships, credit facility reporting, and intercompany funding, escalating covenant and liquidity matters to the CFO.

Systems and Process Improvement

Lead the finance workstreams of the ERP implementation - requirements, chart of accounts design, data migration, UAT, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization - through the transition from QuickBooks.
Collaborate with supporting the Plant Controller and Senior Vice President Operations, operationalize standard costing in the make-to-order manufacturing environment, including BOM accuracy, overhead absorption, and variance analysis.
Drive process automation and continuous improvement of the close, reporting cadence, and documentation base to support margin improvement.

Leadership and Team Development

Manage, mentor, and scale the accounting team; foster a culture of accountability, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration.
Develop the Assistant Controller on a defined succession track toward financial controller-level ownership of the close; establish SOPs, training milestones, and cross-training pairs.
Build a documented and defensible finance function.

Strategic Partnership and CFO Redundancy

Act as the CFO’s deputy: represent Finance with the board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as delegated, and assume the CFO’s operating responsibilities in the CFO’s absence.
Support M&A activity - diligence, integration, and acquisition accounting - including vendor due diligence and quality of earnings readiness.
Support international expansion structuring (Middle East and beyond) with external advisors as it progresses.
Collaborate with the sales, operations, and engineering teams, to be a Business Partner supporting financial decision making, cost savings initiatives, and strategic decision making

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Audit-Ready Financial Reporting:
Consolidated IFRS reporting is delivered accurately and on schedule, with a clean external audit and no material adjustments or control deficiencies.
Scalable, Audit-Ready Finance Function:
Strong controls, clear documentation, and a successfully implemented ERP that position the business well.
Seamless CFO Continuity and Team Succession:
The VP Finance is trusted by the Board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as the CFO’s deputy, while the Assistant Controller progresses to independent ownership of the close.

THE INDIVIDUAL

Given the pivotal role this individual will be expected to play in achieving the strategic objectives of the company and in supporting the success of the organization, it is essential that the successful candidate possess the following education, experience, competencies and attributes:

Education

Strong working knowledge of IFRS is required, including the application of complex technical accounting standards.
Knowledge of U.S. GAAP or cross-border reporting experience would be considered an asset.
Commitment to ongoing professional development, particularly in IFRS, tax, and financial systems.

Experience

A minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including senior leadership responsibility for the accounting and reporting function.
Demonstrated expertise in IFRS, including consolidated reporting across multiple entities, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and preparation of technical accounting positions.

Track record of building and strengthening internal controls, accounting policies, and finance processes.

Nice-to-have:

Experience in a private equity-backed or sponsor-owned organization, vendor due diligence, or quality of earnings processes.

Experience managing banking and credit facility relationships, including covenant compliance.
Involvement in M&A activity, acquisition accounting, or international expansion.

Competencies and Knowledge

Business Partnership:

. Notre organisation est en pleine croissance et transforme son industrie tout en misant sur une culture de collaboration et de plaisir au travail. Si vous êtes reconnu(e) pour votre sens de l'organisation, votre rigueur et votre capacité à mobiliser les gens, nous aimerions vous rencontrer !

Rôle, responsabilités et objectifs

Développer, maintenir et être responsable du modèle financier de projet répondant aux exigences des prêteurs, ainsi que coordonner son audit indépendant.
Diriger l'exécution des financements par dette et par capitaux propres, incluant la préparation du mémorandum d'information, la gestion de la salle de données (data room), les vérifications diligentes des prêteurs et la négociation des feuilles de modalités (term sheets).

Évaluer la bancabilité des baux de locataires, des ententes d'approvisionnement énergétique et des contrats de construction, et intégrer les résultats aux négociations commerciales.

.

new_jobs.description:
Vice President, Supply Chain & Inventory Management

About Delta Group

Delta Group is a Western Canadian wholesale distribution and solutions platform serving waterworks and water infrastructure, agricultural irrigation, pumps and motors, water treatment, wastewater and related markets. Delta combines multi-branch wholesale distribution with specialist technical solutions, engineered systems, projects and service. Through acquisitions and organic growth, the group has an opportunity to integrate supply-chain practices while maintaining the market knowledge and relationships of its operating businesses.

Position mandate

Lead Delta’s end-to-end group supply-chain strategy, with executive accountability for procurement, inventory investment and quality, demand planning, vendor economics, replenishment and network efficiency. Build one disciplined operating framework across multiple companies and branches without impairing customer service or project execution. This is an operational change-leadership position, not simply a senior purchasing appointment. This role can be based in Calgary or Chilliwack, BC.

Group supply-chain strategy and governance

Design and implement group-wide policies for inventory, purchasing, approvals, stock allocation and supplier engagement.
Clarify central versus local authority, escalation rules, exception management and performance accountability.
Partner closely with General Managers, Finance, sales and operations; lead monthly supply-chain performance reviews.
Integrate acquired businesses and branch practices into a scalable operating model.

Inventory investment, productivity and controls

Own group inventory productivity, target-setting and action plans by branch, segment, category and SKU.
Drive reduction of excess, obsolete, slow-moving and duplicate inventory through transfers, vendor returns, disposition and prevention.
Set service-sensitive reorder points, safety stocks, inventory classifications and replenishment policies.
Establish consistent cycle counts, inventory accuracy and inventory ownership controls; coordinate valuation and reserves with Finance.
Protect strategic, seasonal and critical long-lead stock while improving inventory turns and cash generation.

Procurement and supplier management

Coordinate category strategy, purchasing scale, approval limits and controls for committed purchases.
Negotiate supplier terms, pricing, rebates, freight, returns, vendor-managed/consignment arrangements and service commitments.
Implement supplier scorecards and contingency planning for critical products and manufacturers.
Improve purchase-order visibility, interbranch-first decisions and special-order controls; prevent unsupported speculative buys.
Maintain the relationships needed to protect exclusive lines and the commercial advantage of Delta’s technical product portfolios.

Demand planning and major projects

Create rolling forecasting processes using sales patterns, seasonality, known projects and credible customer commitments.
Differentiate recurring wholesale replenishment from project-specific purchasing for pivots, pipe, pumps and engineered packages.
Coordinate purchasing with project managers, installation schedules, deposits and supplier lead times.
Manage cancellations, unallocated project material, foreign-exchange and supply risks through clear ownership and exit plans.

Warehousing, distribution and logistics

Evaluate branch stocking, regional hubs, stock transfers, warehousing productivity and freight economics.
Standardize receiving, storage, picking, shipping and transfers where it creates measurable value.
Build evidence-based business cases for any warehouse consolidation, logistics outsourcing or network redesign.

Systems, master data and analytics

Serve as executive business owner for supply-chain processes.
Establish item-master governance: duplicates, naming, UOMs, vendor references, product attributes, inactive SKUs and status.
Build reliable dashboards for aging, turns, fill rate, demand accuracy, outstanding POs, project stock and supplier performance.
Drive practical system-based replenishment and useful automation rather than spreadsheets without accountability.

Working capital and financial accountability

Develop annual and rolling plans for inventory cash release, purchasing efficiencies and inventory-related operating costs.
Coordinate with VP Finance on cash forecasting, open commitments, vendor terms and independently verified savings.
Evaluate investments against inventory carrying cost, service levels, gross margin, liquidity and project risks.
Report monthly to the CEO with financial outcomes, constraints and corrective actions.

People leadership and transformation

Assess and develop existing branch purchasing, inventory and supply-chain employees; recommend an appropriate group structure.
Hire, coach and hold accountable functional leaders and analysts as approved.
Work constructively with GMs while challenging unsupported inventory and purchasing decisions.
Lead branch-level adoption through training, site visits, clear metrics and consistent follow-through.

Required experience and qualifications

12–15+ years of relevant progression in supply chain, inventory, procurement or wholesale distribution operations, including at least five in a senior multi-branch leadership role.
Demonstrable responsibility for material inventory investment across multiple branches, with quantified improvements in turns, aged inventory, cash flow and service.
Strong track record in vendor negotiations, category strategy, purchase controls and operational change after acquisitions.
Commercial understanding of distribution gross margin, inventory carrying cost, cash conversion, stockouts and service economics.
Hands-on experience implementing effective ERP-based replenishment and master-data management.
Ability to lead effectively through influence and formal authority in decentralized technical distribution businesses.
Relevant degree or equivalent operating experience; SCMP, CSCP or CPIM an asset; regular Western Canadian travel required.

Preferred background

Industrial, waterworks, plumbing, pump and motor, agricultural equipment, irrigation, electrical or HVAC wholesale distribution; acquisition integration; regional distribution network optimization; and balancing project procurement with standard branch replenishment.
Leadership profile
Commercially astute, financially disciplined and decisive; credible at branch and warehouse level; analytically strong, capable of difficult conversations with respected GMs, and equally focused on supplier relationships, customer service and sustainable cash release. Comfortable with ambiguous data but unwilling to accept unsupported conclusions.

Key measures of success

Inventory investment and turns by business, branch and category, adjusted for commercial conditions and service needs.
Aged, obsolete and duplicate stock reduction; inventory accuracy and shrinkage.
Working-capital release and annualized procurement/freight/rebate savings validated by Finance.
Customer fill rates, on-time delivery, backorders and project material availability.
Purchasing compliance, forecasting reliability, supplier performance and inventory transfer effectiveness.
Business Central item-master quality, supply-chain reporting and adoption of replenishment processes.
Strength and accountability of supply-chain leadership and branch operating practices.

First-year priorities

First 30 days: establish validated baselines, purchasing commitment visibility, risk/opportunity ranking and assessment of current team. By 90 days: institute buying authority, interbranch-first controls, aged-inventory program and CEO dashboard. Months 4–6: demonstrate measurable cash release, supplier and forecasting improvements. By 12 months: deliver sustained financial and service outcomes and an approved second-year improvement plan. Specific financial targets will be agreed with the CEO and VP Finance after verifying opening conditions.

Why join Delta

The opportunity is to shape the supply-chain economics of a substantial Western Canadian technical distribution platform, turn scale into meaningful procurement and inventory advantage, and build a disciplined, scalable organization. The role carries senior leadership visibility, operating influence and direct accountability for measurable results.

Overview

The High‑Risk Portfolio Management Team (HRPMT) enhances CCB’s overall risk oversight capabilities by providing specialized expertise, advisory support, and strategic guidance for accounts exhibiting deteriorating financial performance, emerging risk indicators, or complex credit concerns. Unlike traditional credit roles, HRPMT operates in a consulting and advisory capacity
, supporting the commercial banking lines of business with expert insights to strengthen the management of high‑risk, watch‑list, and impaired accounts.

The team works closely with relationship managers, credit partners, and leadership to ensure early identification of risk, informed decision‑making, and strong discipline around the oversight of vulnerable segments of the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Specialized Risk Assessment & Advisory Support

Conducts advanced financial analysis and risk assessments of clients demonstrating signs of weakness or deterioration, providing the LOB with actionable insights and recommended risk‑mitigation strategies.
Offers guidance on appropriate structures, terms, and risk controls for high‑risk accounts, ensuring alignment with bank policies, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Advises on complex or distressed credit situations, including covenant breaches, liquidity concerns, operational challenges, and industry‑driven pressures.
Supports LOB teams with strategies for managing watch‑list, impaired, and emerging‑risk accounts, including exit strategies, recovery pathways, and restructuring options.

High‑Risk Portfolio Oversight

Performs enhanced portfolio monitoring to detect early‑warning signals, covenant non‑compliance, or deteriorating credit trends.
Evaluates portfolio‑level performance indicators and risk concentrations, escalating concerns where appropriate and recommending corrective actions.
Assesses the overall quality of risk management practices across the high‑risk portfolio, identifying gaps and recommending improvements.

Subject Matter Expertise & Consultancy

Operates as a specialist resource to senior leaders and frontline teams, supporting decision‑making on complex or ambiguous credit scenarios.
Provides expertise for the review of high‑risk transactions, challenging underlying assumptions, and advising on risk‑aligned alternatives.
Engages with internal stakeholders to ensure consistency in the management of high‑risk exposures across the enterprise.

Governance, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Strengthens discipline and transparency around watch‑list and impaired account management procedures.
Implements adjustments to risk oversight strategies in response to shifting market, economic, or client‑specific conditions.
Contributes to enterprise initiatives that enhance risk governance, improve monitoring capabilities, and support proactive portfolio management.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partners closely with Commercial banking stakeholders to support their management of deteriorating clients while maintaining LOB ownership of BAU underwriting and client relationships.
Supports senior leadership with insights, analysis, and recommendations to inform capital allocation decisions and risk appetite considerations.
Engages with industry peers and internal networks to stay informed on emerging risks, competitive trends, and evolving best practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience in credit, lending, restructuring, portfolio management, or financial analysis within a corporate or banking environment.
Strong credit qualifications, including deep knowledge of commercial credit structures, deteriorating‑credit dynamics, and high‑risk portfolio management practices.
Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred (Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field).
Demonstrated ability to assess complex financial situations, identify risks, and recommend solutions aligned with risk appetite and enterprise policies.
Proven capability to operate in an advisory role, influence stakeholders, and provide expertise in non‑routine, ambiguous, or sensitive credit situations.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgment under pressure.

Establish commercial targets and translate company objectives into measurable team goals and action plans.
Identify new business opportunities, market trends, and strategic relationships that support sustainable growth.

Team Leadership & Management

Lead, manage, and develop a team of up to 12 professionals across Marketing, Partnerships, Alliances, Lead Generation, Regional Sales, Account Management, Client Experience, and Claims.
Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and measurable targets for team members.
Provide coaching, guidance, and regular performance reviews to drive accountability and team effectiveness.

Enterprise Sales & Business Development

Oversee regional sales teams responsible for Ontario, Quebec, and the rest of Canada.
Lead the full B2B sales cycle, including prospecting, lead qualification, client presentations, proposals, negotiations, and closing deals.
Develop sales strategies, regional targets, and territory priorities.
